editorial:
You wake up with no memory on a dark ship, and that alone is enough to make your skin crawl. Pandorum drops you into a nightmare where two crew members, Bower and Payton, try to piece together who they are while crawling through a massive spacecraft that feels empty but definitely is not. The setup is simple but strong: no names, no mission details, no sense of time, just flickering lights, strange noises, and the growing feeling that something is hunting them. The movie leans into mystery first, then slowly turns into survival horror as the truth about the ship and its passengers comes out. It has that late-night, lights-off energy that makes you want to keep watching even when you want to look away.

Ben Foster and Dennis Quaid carry the tension well, especially when the story shifts from quiet confusion to fast, brutal action. The creature designs are creepy, the ship looks worn and believable, and the pacing rarely lets you breathe. On the downside, some twists feel rushed, and a few characters are more plot devices than people. Still, if you enjoy dark sci-fi with monsters, mystery, and a big final reveal, this is a solid pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray if you want the full home-theater experience.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, Bower reaches the bridge and learns the ship has already arrived at Tanis and is resting on the ocean floor. The hunters are descendants of the original passengers, changed by years in the dark. Payton is revealed to be Gallo, the crew member who went mad and caused the chaos. Bower and Nadia escape in a pod, launch to the surface, and see sunlight and land, proving they have finally reached their new home.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves dark sci-fi horror with twists.
